page: Vultr vcg-a40-24c-120g-48vram is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Dedicated Metal GPU family. It features an Intel x86_64 CPU architecture with 24 dedicated vCPUs and 120.0 GB of system memory, yielding 5.0 GB of RAM per core. The storage configuration consists of a 1400 GB local NVMe SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Although NVIDIA is specified as the GPU manufacturer, the active GPU count is listed as 0.0 in the configuration.

No benchmark data is available for this specific server configuration, meaning direct performance comparisons cannot be quantified. From a hardware class perspective, the dedicated allocation of 24 Intel vCPUs and 120.0 GB RAM provides a stable, non-shared resource pool. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage ensures local data access compared to network-attached storage alternatives. The qualitative cost efficiency of this server is defined by its dedicated resource model, which eliminates noisy-neighbor issues but carries a higher resource-density cost compared to shared-core virtual machines.

This server configuration is designed for workloads requiring dedicated Intel CPU resources, moderate memory capacity, and local NVMe storage. Suitable applications include database hosting, general-purpose backend services, application development environments, and localized data processing tasks that do not require active GPU acceleration.
